WebsitesView.title: Websites
WebsitesView.subtitle: Customer portal: the websites through which customers reach their account
WebsitesView.intro: Every HugoCMS website where customers sign in gets its access and settings here. A HugoShop is assigned to a website in the sales channels.
WebsitesView.name: Name
WebsitesView.created: Website created. It stays switched off until it is set up.
WebsitesView.activeHint: Switched off, the access accepts no requests from this website.
WebsitesView.settingsRejected: Not saved: {fields}. The backend does not know these fields yet – the database update is probably missing (sign in again).
WebsitesView.saveError: The settings could not be saved.
WebsitesView.loadError: The websites could not be loaded.
WebsitesView.deleteConfirm: Delete website “{name}”? Sessions and open activations go with it; invoice links are kept.
WebsitesView.noChannels: No sales channel — customer account, invoices and contact only.
WebsitesView.installHint: Transfers templates, widgets and the proxy to HugoCMS and has the website built.
WebsitesView.installNeeded: This change only reaches the website after “Install package”.

fields.activatePage_help: Page where existing customers activate their customer account. Empty = freischalten/.
fields.contactMailTo_help: E-mail address that receives contact form requests. Empty = the company’s sender address.
fields.hugocms_help: Connection to HugoCMS, which builds and publishes this website.
fields.hugocmsUrl_help: Web address for remote access to HugoCMS via the website.
fields.publicKey_help: Secret key with which the website identifies itself to OpensourceERP.
fields.allowedOrigins_help: Only needed if the website calls OpensourceERP directly without the proxy — otherwise leave empty.
fields.backendUrl: Web address of the customer portal access
fields.backendUrl_help: Address at which the website reaches OpensourceERP, for example https://erp.example.com/portal/.
fields.baseUrl_help: Address visitors use to open the website, for example https://www.example.com/.
fields.invoicePage_help: Page of the website that shows an invoice. Empty = rechnung/.
fields.templateSet_help: Design of the portal pages; “Standard” suits most websites.
fields.grants_help: HugoCMS decides where OpensourceERP may write (project settings → OpensourceERP connection). Shown here for reference only; the transfer applies the grants every time.
fields.signingKey_help: Enter it in HugoCMS under project settings → OpensourceERP connection. OpensourceERP then transfers the proxy and the 404 page itself. Applies to all websites of this installation.
fields.hugocmsUrl: Web address for HugoCMS remote access
fields.hugocmsKey_help: Access key that HugoCMS generated for this website.
fields.loginPage_help: Page with the login form. Default anmelden/.
fields.registerPage_help: Page where new customers create an account. Default registrieren/.
fields.accountPage_help: Overview of the customer account; profile, addresses and invoices live below it. Default konto/.
fields.contactPage_help: Page with the contact form. Default kontakt/.
fields.portalPath_help: Common start of all portal pages, for example /kunden/ or /kundenportal/. Default /kunden/.
fields.activationEnabled_help: Existing customers without a customer account can have access set up via WhatsApp. Off = no link, no page. Default: off.
fields.documentsInvoices_help: The customer sees their invoices and downloads them as PDF. Default: on.
fields.documentsOrders_help: The customer sees their orders (order confirmations) with PDF.
fields.documentsQuotations_help: The customer sees the quotations they received, with PDF.
fields.documentsDeliveryOrders_help: The customer sees their delivery notes with PDF, without prices.
fields.documentsReclamations_help: The customer sees their complaints with the reason per item. No PDF.
fields.documentsShopOrders_help: Shop extension only: orders from the online shop as their own tab with payment and delivery status. Default: on.

WebsitesView.proxyHint: The website reaches OpensourceERP through the proxy /portal-api/ in the package — or through a reverse proxy that sets the header X-Portal-Key.

backendTest.INVALID: Not a valid address: {url} — expected something like https://erp.example.com/portal/
backendTest.IS_HUGOCMS: This is the HugoCMS address ({url}). The OpensourceERP portal access belongs here, e.g. https://erp.example.com/portal/ — locally http://localhost:8000/portal/.
backendTest.NO_KEY: The website has no key yet.
backendTest.OK: The OpensourceERP portal access responds, the key matches “{name}”.
backendTest.OK_OLD: The OpensourceERP portal access responds and accepts the key; this version cannot tell the website.
backendTest.OTHER_WEBSITE: The portal access responds, but the key belongs to another website: “{name}”.
backendTest.HUGOCMS: The response came from HugoCMS instead of the OpensourceERP portal access. Via the website the address transferred last applies — after a correction, save and run “Install package”.
backendTest.KEY_REJECTED: The portal access rejected the key — check the website key; via the website the key transferred last applies.
backendTest.PROXY_NOT_CONFIGURED: The proxy runs but cannot find oserp-portal/config.json or it is incomplete — run “Install package”.
backendTest.FOREIGN: Something other than OpensourceERP answers at {url} (HTTP {status}). The address probably points to a foreign page or another service — check the web address.
backendTest.NOT_FOUND:
Nothing answers at {url} (error 404). Either the proxy is not on the website yet, or the website address is wrong.
Next steps: 1. Check that “Web address of the website” is the home page as visitors open it. 2. Run “Install package” so the proxy gets onto the website. 3. Then check again here. Note: often the website project’s config.json lacks the entries for the package — the info icon shows which.
backendTest.WEBSITE_INACTIVE: The website is switched off. The connection works, but login, registration and account tell visitors “customer portal not available”. To release it, turn on “Website enabled” at the top of the card.

WebsitesView.hugocmsShopOff: In HugoCMS the online shop is not enabled for this website — turn on “Online shop on this website” in the project settings under “OpensourceERP connection”. Until then the shop run transfers no product pages.

help.baseUrl:
The website address is the baseURL of the Hugo site as the browser calls it — with https:// and a trailing slash.

OpensourceERP derives two things from it: the location of the proxy (<address>/portal-api/) that the website widgets call, and the links in e-mails and WhatsApp messages (invoice, activate account).

A path belongs here only if the whole Hugo site lives in a subdirectory, e.g. https://company.example/portal/ — then its baseURL ends the same way and Hugo places the proxy under that path.

Not meant is the subpage holding the portal pages (e.g. /customers/login/). Those pages belong under “Pages of the website”.

Check: “Test connection”, third step “Via the website” calls exactly <address>/portal-api/.
help.publicKey:
The website key is the secret with which the website identifies itself to the OpensourceERP portal access. It determines tenant and website there — so every website needs its own.

Normally only the /portal-api/ proxy on the web server sees it: OpensourceERP writes it with “Install package” into oserp-portal/config.json, outside the public directory. Customers’ browsers never see it.

If your own reverse proxy replaces the proxy, it sets the header X-Portal-Key with the same value.

Generate a new key: icon at the right of the field. Then “Install package”, otherwise the website still works with the old one.
help.allowedOrigins:
Allowed origins are needed only if the OpensourceERP portal access is called directly from the browser — i.e. without the /portal-api/ proxy and without your own reverse proxy.

Then requests come from a different address than OpensourceERP itself, and the browser demands a CORS clearance. Enter the website addresses here, comma-separated, with scheme: https://www.example.com, https://example.com.

If the website runs via the proxy as intended, leave the field empty: browser and proxy share the same address, there is nothing to clear.

Security: every listed address may open sessions with the website key — enter only your own websites.
help.backendUrl:
The address of the portal access is the public entry point of OpensourceERP for customers: the backend/portal/ directory of the installation, for example https://erp.example.com/portal/ — locally with scripts/dev.sh http://localhost:8000/portal/.

The /portal-api/ proxy on the website forwards all widget requests there: login, account, invoices and, with a shop, cart and checkout. “Install package” writes the address together with the website key into oserp-portal/config.json.

Not here: the HugoCMS address (…/cms-api/, HugoCMS card) and the address of the website itself.

An empty field is prefilled with the address OpensourceERP is currently called at. Behind a reverse proxy this is the externally visible address — it must be reachable from the website’s web server.

“Test connection” checks in three steps: input, directly from OpensourceERP, via the website.
help.hugocmsUrl:
HugoCMS is the program the website is maintained and built with. OpensourceERP sends it the customer portal package and then has the website rebuilt. For that it needs a web address at which HugoCMS is reachable from outside.

HugoCMS shows this address itself: in the project settings of the website under “OpensourceERP connection”. It ends in /cms-api/, for example https://www.example.com/cms-api/. Best copy it from there.

The address must start with https://, otherwise HugoCMS refuses the connection. The only exception is a test on the same machine.

Check: the button “Check connection and fetch grants” in this card.
help.hugocmsKey:
With this key OpensourceERP identifies itself to HugoCMS. It applies to this one website only.

It is generated in HugoCMS: project settings of the website → “OpensourceERP connection” → “Generate key”. HugoCMS shows it in full exactly once — copy it then and paste it here. Later HugoCMS shows only the last four characters, which lets you check that both sides hold the same key.

If the key is lost, generate a new one in HugoCMS and replace it here. The old one is then no longer valid.
help.invoicePage:
Customers receive a link to their invoice in e-mails. This link leads to a page of the website that shows the invoice — its path goes here, for example /invoice/.

The page is created in HugoCMS with the “shop-invoice” building block on it. If the field is empty, OpensourceERP uses rechnung/.

The link contains a secret code, so guests without a customer account can see their invoice too.
help.activatePage:
The link that existing customers receive via WhatsApp leads to this page, for example freischalten/. Without a leading slash the entry is appended to the customer portal directory.

“Install package” puts the page from the template set onto the website; your own page at the same address takes precedence. If the field is empty, OpensourceERP uses freischalten/.

The same path belongs in the WhatsApp template “Activate customer account” as the button address.
help.templateSet:
The template set determines how login, customer account, invoices and contact form look on the website. “Standard” adapts to the website’s look and is sufficient in most cases.

A developer can create custom sets in the company’s template directory under portal/; they then appear here for selection.

After switching, run “Install package” so the website receives the new templates.
help.contactMailTo:
When a customer fills in the contact form on the website, OpensourceERP sends the request as an e-mail to this address.

If the field is empty, the request goes to the company’s sender address from the company configuration.

Multiple recipients are not supported — use a shared mailbox or a distribution list instead.
help.pages:
At these addresses “Install package” creates the portal pages on the website — ready, with the matching building block. This needs the entry for oserp-portal/content in the website project’s config.json (see the help at “Test connection”).

The address is given from the root of the website, with a slash at the start and end, for example /kunden/anmelden/. The subpages of the account (profile, addresses, invoices, with a shop the payment method, with vehicles the vehicles) hang below the customer account address.

The widgets use the same addresses for their links, and OpensourceERP for the links in e-mails and WhatsApp messages. To design a page yourself, create your own page in HugoCMS at the same address — it takes precedence over the page from the package.

After a change, run “Install package”.

The customer portal directory is the common start: a page without a leading slash (e.g. anmelden/) hangs below it — /kunden/ and anmelden/ become /kunden/anmelden/. To use a different directory, changing this one field is enough. A page with a leading slash (e.g. /login/) stands on its own.
help.activationEnabled:
Customers who have already bought from you but do not have a customer account yet can set up access themselves: on the website they enter their mobile number and postcode or customer number and receive a link via WhatsApp.

When switched on, “Install package” creates the “Activate account” page on the website, and the login and registration pages show the link to it. The link can also be sent from the customer file.

When switched off there is neither page nor link, and activation requests are rejected. After switching, please run “Install package” so the website receives the new state.

Sending via WhatsApp requires a configured WhatsApp access and the template “Activate customer account” approved by Meta.
help.documents:
On the “Documents” page of the customer account the customer sees the documents ticked here, each type as its own tab, with date, amount, status and items. Invoices, orders, quotations and delivery notes offer a PDF download; OpensourceERP does not print complaints yet, so that button is missing there.

Default: invoices only. The ticks take effect immediately, no “Install package” is needed. If nothing is ticked, the page shows a notice instead of a list.

All documents of the customer record are shown, not only those created through the website, so a workshop customer also sees the workshop invoice. With the shop extension, shop invoices additionally show payment and delivery status.

With the shop extension there is also “Orders (online shop)”: the invoices from the online shop as their own tab with payment and delivery status. When it is switched on, these invoices no longer appear under “Invoices”, so each document is listed once.

mountsHelp.title: Entries for the website’s config.json
mountsHelp.text: For Hugo to pick up the proxy, templates and widgets from the package, the “module” section of the Hugo project’s config.json must look like this — the first entries are the website’s usual directories, the last four belong to the package:
mountsHelp.after:
The file lives in the website’s project directory on the web server; in HugoCMS it can be edited under “All files”. Then run “Install package” and check again here.

Without these entries the package reaches HugoCMS, but Hugo copies none of it into the built website — the proxy then answers with error 404.
